children: Brazil's central government recorded a primary surplus of 52.3 billion reais ($9.25 billion) in October, Treasury data showed on Friday, above the 47.6 billion reais surplus forecast by economists polled by Reuters.
In the 12 months through October, Latin America's largest economy posted a primary deficit of 35.6 billion reais, equivalent to 0.27% of its gross domestic product (GDP).
The strong monthly result was driven by a 5.6% real increase in net revenue, amid record tax collection and a sharp rise in oil royalty and crude sales revenue as oil prices climbed
Total expenditure fell 0.2% in real terms from a year earlier, mainly reflecting lower healthcare spending, the Treasury said
Government officials said earlier this week they expect to end the year with an effective primary deficit of around 0.5% of GDP
The formal 2026 target calls for a primary surplus of 0.25% of GDP for the central government
However, Brazil's fiscal framework allows certain expenditures to be excluded from the target calculation and includes a tolerance band of 0.25 percentage point in either direction
